The statement least likely to follow from Savigny’s Volksgeist is that a people’s spirit is too uniform and abstract to shape particular legal rules, so those rules connect to cultural character only loosely and incidentally. For Savigny, law is the organic expression of a particular people’s shared consciousness and grows, like language, through custom and later juristic articulation. A view of law as sovereign command, or as a universal code deduced from pure reason and imposed without regard to national history, is equally alien to that notion.

CONFIDENCE: 82
